advances: A scalar implication for balanced finite coefficient lists with a fixed negative unit.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
For each $d\ge1$, the domain of coefficient vectors is closed and bounded and contains $(-1,1,0,\ldots,0)$. Coupling the exponentials gives almost-sure convergence of the signed sums when coefficients converge. Each limiting sum has an independent continuous term $-E_0$, so its probability of equality at zero is zero. Bounded convergence gives continuity of the sign probability. Denote its attained minimum by $c_d$. Padding by one zero shows $c_{d+1}\le c_d$.

Suppose the weak conclusion fails at dimension $d_0$, so $c_{d_0}<c$, or that the strict conclusion fails under the strict premise, so $c_{d_0}\le c$. Choose a minimizing vector for every $d\ge d_0$. The capped minimizer classification excludes its all-unit-negative alternative because it has probability at least $1/2>c$. For the all-unit-positive alternative with $k$ positive phases, the residual negative coefficients have total $k-1$, each is at most one, and one distinguished negative unit is fixed. The saturated exact gamma infimum bounds this probability below by $G_{k,0}$, including $k=1$. It therefore excludes that alternative in either the weak or the strict argument.

The remaining classification gives positive coefficients $(1,\ldots,1,p_d)$ with $k_d$ units and negative magnitudes $(1,b_d,\ldots,b_d)$ with $m_d$ copies of $b_d$, where $p_d,b_d\in(0,1)$ and $m_db_d=k_d+p_d-1$. There are no zero coefficients, so $k_d+m_d=d-1$. If $k_d$ is unbounded, a subsequence with $k_d\to\infty$ has $c_d\to1/2$ by the uniform sign limit in the two-limit lemma, which contradicts $c_d\le c_{d_0}\le c$. The uniformity allows any accompanying $m_d$, including $m_d\to\infty$.

Otherwise pass to a constant-$k$ subsequence and then one on which $p_d\to p\in[0,1]$. Along it $m_d\to\infty$ by the count identity. The fixed-$k$ sign limit gives $c_d\to G_{k,p}$. Under the weak premise this is impossible because $c_d\le c_{d_0}<c\le G_{k,p}$. Under the strict premise it is impossible because $c_d\le c<G_{k,p}$. This proves both assertions using attained minima in each finite dimension.
statement:
Let $c<1/2$ be real. For every integer $k\ge1$ and $p\in[0,1]$, set
$$
G_{k,p}=\Pr(X_k+pE_+\ge E_-+k+p-1),
$$
where $X_k\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ and $E_+,E_-$ are unit-mean exponentials, with all terms independent. Suppose $G_{k,p}\ge c$ for all such $k,p$. Then for every integer $d\ge1$ and all $a_0,\ldots,a_d\in[-1,1]$ with $a_0=-1$ and $\sum_{i=0}^d a_i=0$, independent unit-mean exponentials $E_0,\ldots,E_d$ satisfy
$$
\Pr\!\left(\sum_{i=0}^d a_iE_i\ge0\right)\ge c.
$$
If $G_{k,p}>c$ for every such $k,p$, the resulting sign probability is strictly greater than $c$ for every finite coefficient list in this domain.
title: A deterministic-threshold reduction for capped signed exponential probabilities
